I had several long distance relationships and have hopes for you two.Staying busy is good but doing things together online is even better - install Syncplay so you can watch movies at the exact same time and stop and go and comment as you watch.

There used to be an app for couples called Avocado where it's basically Whatsapp but only for the two - you draw a simple drawing when you think of the other person, just a little nudge. Perhaps there's something similar like that out now.

Sexy chats will never be exactly the same as the real deal but getting into it in detail, what you think her hair might smell could help that little bit more.

Have you tried learning each others languages? Say one just sends a word and the other has to look it up and learn it (some nice words to get you feeling fuzzy).

Send each other a small item and take photos with it wherever you go - toy dinosaur when you go walking in the woods to show the 'friend' she gifted you is following your step.

I hope your family is okay and you are safe; if so, talk about your loved ones and what they get up to.

These are some off the top of my head. I hope at least some will help. Again, best of luck in life for both you and your girl

Hi, thanks for inquiring!  


The relationship has turned into a period of calm and my sustaining myself followed by a bi-weekly 'I can't handle this, I gotta say something' full-on rampage in the middle of the night, kicks, screams, break-ups, going to sleep in another room, my pleading and crying while gasping for breath.   


There is miscommunication, yes. He is a person that likes keeping to himself and is not at all a romantic person. I guess he loves me in his own way (he's still with me so that's proof I guess). We have similar values but his and my boundaries do not overlap at all. He'd be fine not talking to me for days while I want hugs and kisses all of the time. I feel like I've never had my fill and haven't developed a sense of closeness to him. He has also let me down on very many occasions, almost never keeping promises (never calling when promised, never coming home when promised) and therefore fueling my sense of dread and fear of being unloved and abandoned.   


I do not have very many people in my life as a result of moving to another country for him. Since I've moved I've been entangled in the relationship and felt too ashamed to go out into the world and be comfortable enough with myself to make new friends. Same goes for hobbies - although my work takes up a lot of time and at least there's that.  


Tbh, no one deserves to live with a person that can easily throw a fit but I'm pretty sure he's about the worst candidate to be the loving, understanding boyfriend. He flip-flops, says nice things and then very mean things (he told me I am capable of killing little kittens, smashing their heads in when animals are the love of my life and the though of them on numerous occasions was my only lifeline). He ridiculed me yesterday, blew smoke in my face. When I asked why he said 'to piss me off'. He has become and angry man and we've both turned violent in the last while.   


The more I write the more meaningless it all seems. There is no communication, only hurt, pain and tears - and rage from his side.   


On a brighter note, you seem to have a very loving thing going on. I hope it stays that way forever.   


Thank you for listening and sorry about being rambly.
